title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers a request of the provisioner contract with, application/json, as the integration contract's refusal, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/refusal.schema.json. The codes the starter meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking, for each cause that refusal lists, a replay under the replay rule of https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json among them: it tells the starter nothing about which cause applied, and the starter never takes it as the pool's access key being revoked; 403 forbidden, a request outside the key's rights, a claim whose pool_id is not the key's node pool, and a request naming a dispatch_id that is unknown or of another node pool than the key's, each with the same signed body as an unknown id, so nobody learns whether an id exists: the signature with the pool's access key and this check authorise a request, not the id, and the control plane decides it before any 409 or 410; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 no_gateway, a claim when the choice of the key's node pool resolves to no gateway, claim.schema.json; 409 machine_exists, a release after the control plane accepted dispatched for the dispatch, or after the machine redeemed the dispatch's run code, release.schema.json; 409 machine_log_exists, a machine log for a dispatch that has one already, machine-log.schema.json; 409 lease_expired, a first dispatched of a dispatch, or a release, naming a stale dispatch, one whose lease lapsed because neither dispatched nor the redemption of its run code came before lease_until, until the control plane ends it, as claim-answer.schema.json describes, on which the starter stops the machine it created for that dispatch, if it created one, and never a dispatch whose run code was redeemed, because such a dispatch never goes stale; 410 gone, a request naming a dispatch that ended: at its release, as release.schema.json describes, when the machine has not redeemed the run code within 15 minutes of the claim, or when the control plane ends the work the dispatch is for, claim-answer.schema.json, except a machine log, which the control plane accepts after the dispatch ends; on a 410 to a dispatched, the starter sends the machine log and deletes the machine, dispatched.schema.json; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the starter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry. Beside the codes any request may meet, 401, 400, 404, 413, 415 and 429, each request's refusals apply in this order, the first that applies: a claim, claim.schema.json: 403 forbidden, 409 no_gateway; a dispatched, dispatched.schema.json: 403 forbidden, 410 gone, 409 lease_expired; a release, release.schema.json: 403 forbidden, 410 gone, 409 machine_exists, 409 lease_expired; a machine log, machine-log.schema.json: 403 forbidden, 409 machine_log_exists. A machine log is never refused 410 gone or 409 lease_expired: the control plane accepts it before or after the dispatch ends. No refusal is tied to a policy. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and the starter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the starter changes no state: no dispatch, no machine, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the starter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A member this schema does not define is refused.
